Subject: AcmeHealth - private VPC data flow & PII handling (post-call)

Hi Jose / ACME Security team,

Thanks for the time today — appreciate the detailed walkthrough of your use case and the sensitivity around PHI/PII and logging. Per our call, I wanted to capture the TL;DR and next steps so we have a single reference for procurement and your security review.

Summary of what we heard:
- Workload: patient-facing chat + clinical note summarization; user inputs may include name, DOB, limited medical history (PII/PHI).
- Volume: ~250k requests/month, 90th pct payload length ~1.2k chars.
- Residency: data must remain in AcmeHealth VPC with no persistent egress to external networks for raw input.
- Retention: raw inputs must be retained for 30 days for debugging and then deleted; aggregate logs (non-PII) retained 13 months.
- Audit: you require request/response logging metadata (timestamps, model used, redaction flags) with access controls and exportable audit logs for compliance.

Our proposed private deployment pattern (high level):
1) Private control plane + customer-managed VPC peering or private endpoint. No raw data stored outside your VPC.
2) Model inference happens on dedicated pods inside the VPC (or via a VPC-hosted runtime) — KV cache kept in-memory; optional diskless mode for air-gapped on-prem setups.
3) Configurable logging: we can ship only metadata (request id, model, token counts, latency) out-of-band; raw inputs can be stored in a customer-managed S3 bucket with lifecycle policies you control.

Attachments: I attached a diagram (redwood-vpc-dataflow-diagram.pdf) and a short deployment summary and SOC2 evidence checklist we typically share.

Next steps I propose:
- Technical deep-dive with your security/infra team (Vivek from our infra team + Neha from security) to map egress/egress filters and peering options — can we pencil Wed 4/8 or Thu 4/9?
- I'll follow up with a short mutual action plan doc and the SOC2 evidence spreadsheet for you to fill.

Action items for Acme: please share the preferred contact for networking (VPC admin) and whether an air-gapped/on-prem option is required or just private VPC with strict egress controls.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — good recap. A few clarifying questions before we loop infra: 

1) For the "no raw data stored outside your VPC" statement: can you confirm whether any telemetry or model metadata will be sent to Redwood-managed control plane (hosted) for monitoring? If so, is that metadata ever tieable back to patient identifiers?

2) Retention: our legal team will want explicit guarantees (and preferably automation) for the 30-day deletion of raw inputs. Do you provide lifecycle enforcement or do we manage retention entirely on our side?

3) Logging & Audit: we need request/response hashes and an immutable audit trail. Is immutable logging supported and can you export logs to our SIEM via TLS/syslog or S3?

4) Air-gapped: we are evaluating both private VPC and an on-prem air-gapped option for certain regulated pilots. What's the feature parity difference (especially around model updates and monitoring)?

Can you also include any references to your SOC2 controls mapping for logging/retention? I'll share our network contact after confirming with infra.

— Jose

Subject: Re: AcmeHealth - private VPC data flow & PII handling (post-call)

Hi Jose — great questions. Quick answers, and Vivek/Neha can expand on the technical detail in the call: 

1) Control plane telemetry: by default the Redwood control plane collects non-PII telemetry (metrics, token counts, host health). We offer an option to disable hosted telemetry and send metrics to your telemetry endpoint via a push gateway or accept only anonymized metrics. We never link telemetry to patient identifiers unless a customer opts into sending identifiable metadata.

2) Retention & deletion: we recommend customer-managed S3 for raw inputs so your lifecycle policies enforce deletion (we can provide IaC snippets to create lifecycle rules and a sample Lambda that validates deletions). If you require server-side enforcement inside the runtime, we can enable configurable auto-delete after X days — that feature is available on Dedicated/Private installs and can be locked via policy.

3) Logging & audit: we support write-once audit exports to your S3 (WORM-style using S3 Object Lock) or push to your SIEM via TLS endpoint. We also produce cryptographic hashes for request/response pairs if you want immutability verification. Access control is RBAC + IAM integration.

4) Air-gapped parity: air-gapped on-prem gives you full control (no external connectivity) — model updates are done via signed bundles staged by your ops team. Monitoring is limited to in-VPC collectors; remote support is possible via scheduled secure data-transfer windows. Feature parity is high for inference and data controls; hosted features (like Redwood hosted analytics and auto-scaling) are limited or require connector windows.

Attachments: I attached the SOC2 evidence checklist (SOC2-evidence-request.xlsx) and a short deployment summary.

Proposed time for technical deep dive: Wed 4/8 11:00 PT (30m) — suggested participants: Vivek (infra), Neha (security), your VPC/network admin, and Rishi (AE). Does that work?

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks all — adding a few technical notes ahead of the 11:00 PT call to make the conversation productive: 

- Network boundaries: we support two deployment patterns for private VPCs: (A) VPC peering with private endpoints (no internet egress from runtime), (B) VPC-hosted runtime using customer-managed subnets with NAT policies; for (A) egress is blocked unless you explicitly allow specific outbound endpoints.

- Egress controls: we can bind egress to allowlist of IPs/domains. For your air-gapped request, we recommend option (A) + explicit deny-all outbound routes; model artifact updates are done via signed tarball delivered through a secure ops channel.

- Logging controls: runtime supports three tiers: (1) metadata-only (default for high-sensitivity), (2) hashed request/response pairs stored encrypted, (3) full logs to customer S3. We recommend (1) or (2) for PHI; if you choose (2) we can configure server-side encryption + S3 Object Lock for immutability.

- Retention enforcement: if you want enforcement inside the runtime (not just lifecycle in S3), we can enable an auto-delete feature that purges raw inputs after X days; note that enabling auto-delete requires agreement on how long cached KV state is kept for ongoing sessions. We'll put the exact TTL options in the MSA addendum.

- On-prem constraints: for truly air-gapped deployments we provide a deployment bundle and deployment playbook; support is via signed manifests and scheduled offline bundle transfers. Observability is local; we can deliver periodic aggregated telemetry artifacts for offline review.

Pre-call ask (please share before 11:00 PT):
- A basic network diagram showing your VPC subnets and NAT/route table constraints (if you already have one).
- Confirmation if you require S3 Object Lock / WORM for audit logs.

I'll join the call and bring example Terraform snippets and the runtime config that toggles logging tiers.

— Vivek
